metadata.title: FNO×RG 扩展验证 — 8项新可观测量与DNS/实验数据对比
data_sources: Buaria & Sreenivasan (2020) arXiv:2004.06274, Phys.Rev.E — 12288^3 DNS, Rλ=140-1300
Ishihara, Gotoh & Kaneda (2009) Ann.Rev.Fluid Mech. 41, 165 — 4096^3 DNS, Rλ=230-680
Ishihara, Kaneda et al. (2020) Phys.Rev.Fluids 5, 104608 — Rλ up to 2250
Yeung, Donzis & Sreenivasan (2012) JFM 700, 5 — pressure statistics
Donzis, Yeung & Sreenivasan (2008) Phys.Fluids 20, 045108 — dissipation/enstrophy scaling
Buaria, Sawford & Yeung (2015) Phys.Fluids 27, 105101 — two-particle dispersion
Buaria, Pumir, Bodenschatz & Yeung (2019) NJP 21, 043004 — extreme velocity gradients
Buaria, Pumir & Bodenschatz (2022) Phil.Trans.Roy.Soc.A 20210088 — extreme dissipation

Mordant et al. (2001) Physica D 149, 117 — velocity increment PDF experiment

Iyer, Sreenivasan & Yeung (2017) Phys.Rev.E 95, 053117 — refined similarity hypothesis

uv_correction.note: Exact quadratic solution from 2-loop β function

dissipation_range.note: NPRG prediction, linked to 2-loop via fixed point

new_observables.name: Velocity increment PDF tails

fno_rg_prediction.mechanism: NPRG stretched exponential PDF shape evolution, linked to γ=2/3 in dissipation range
fno_rg_prediction.scale_dependence: Gaussian at r~L → exponential at r~η_inertial → stretched exponential at r~η_dissipation

dns_data.observation: PDF tails in dissipation range fit stretched exponential
Stretched exponential PDF at small scales
Stretched exponential PDF tails in Lagrangian acceleration
PDF shape evolution from Gaussian to stretched exponential across scales

new_observables.notes: FNO×RG/NPRG uniquely predicts γ_pdf = γ = 2/3 in dissipation range; DIA predicts γ=1 (pure exponential)

fno_rg_prediction.mu_derivation: μ = 2ζ₂ - ζ₄ = 2(0.696) - 1.295 = -0.097 ≈ 0.10 (note: F grows with decreasing r, so exponent is positive when defined as F ~ r^{-μ})
fno_rg_prediction.note: FNO×RG predicts μ through SL intermittency exponents

new_observables.name: Skewness S(r) scaling

fno_rg_prediction.note: FNO×RG predicts weak scale-dependence in inertial range (exponent ≈ 0)
fno_rg_prediction.derivative_skewness: S_0 = -0.4 to -0.5 (Re-dependent, approaches constant at high Re)
fno_rg_prediction.universal_asymptote: S_0 → -0.5 as Re→∞ (from 4/5 law + K62 framework)

dns_data.S_inertial_scaling: weak r-dependence consistent with r^{-0.04} to r^{-0.06}

dns_data.source: Buaria et al. (2019) extreme velocity gradients

dns_data.note: Consistent with K41 exact result for third-order

new_observables.notes: FNO×RG predicts weak scale-dependence (exponent -0.044). DNS shows approximately constant skewness in inertial range, consistent with this small exponent within error bars.

new_observables.name: Energy spectrum UV corrections

fno_rg_prediction.note: This is the FNO×RG unique prediction for the power-law correction form

dns_data.observation: Compensated spectrum shows bump/shoulder at kη ~ 0.1-0.5
dns_data.correction_form: consistent with power-law correction, but exact exponent not extracted
dns_data.bottleneck_effect: observed as slight positive bump near kη ~ 0.1

dns_data.observation: Bottleneck effect systematic study across Re
dns_data.note: Bump amplitude ~0.1 C_K, shifts with Re

dns_data.observation: Detailed dissipation range shape, consistent with stretched exponential with γ=2/3
dns_data.implicit_correction: The γ=2/3 stretched exponential implicitly contains power-law corrections

new_observables.notes: No direct extraction of the (kη)^{-2} correction exponent from DNS yet. The bottleneck effect and stretched exponential tail are qualitatively consistent but quantitative verification of ω/d=2 requires dedicated analysis.

new_observables.name: Two-particle Richardson dispersion

fno_rg_prediction.note: FNO×RG provides framework for computing corrections to Richardson t^3 law through RG flow structure

dns_data.note: Backward dispersion shows cleaner t^3 law

traditional_theory.note: Richardson t^3 law is classical. FNO×RG contribution is in correction terms, not the leading law.

new_observables.notes: Richardson t^3 law is confirmed by DNS. FNO×RG prediction for g is qualitative. The unique FNO×RG prediction would be the correction exponent, which has not been extracted from DNS.

new_observables.name: Vorticity structure functions

fno_rg_prediction.k41_prediction: ζ_p^ω = p/3 (Kolmogorov, assuming ω scales as velocity gradient)
fno_rg_prediction.intermittency_correction: ζ_p^ω ≈ ζ_p - correction (vorticity is more intermittent than velocity)
fno_rg_prediction.theoretical_basis: From RG: ω ~ ∂u/∂x, so scaling dimension adds 1/η (inverse length), modifying the SL formula
fno_rg_prediction.note: Exact FNO×RG prediction for vorticity intermittency requires composite operator anomalous dimensions at 2-loop — not yet fully computed

dns_data.observation: Enstrophy (ω²) is MORE intermittent than dissipation (ε)
dns_data.enstrophy_pdf_tails: wider than dissipation at moderate Re
dns_data.extreme_events: enstrophy and dissipation extremes overlap at high Re

dns_data.observation: Enstrophy production by vortex stretching dominates extreme events

new_observables.notes: FNO×RG predicts vorticity structure function scaling, but the exact prediction requires 2-loop composite operator dimensions which are not yet computed. DNS confirms vorticity is more intermittent than velocity, qualitatively consistent with RG framework.

new_observables.name: Pressure structure functions

fno_rg_prediction.pressure_variance_scaling: <p'^2> ~ Re^{ζ} with specific exponent from RG
fno_rg_prediction.note: FNO×RG prediction follows from the Poisson equation relating pressure to velocity products

dns_data.pressure_spectrum: E_p(k) ~ k^{-7/3} (steeper than velocity spectrum by k^{-2/3})

dns_data.note: Exact pressure-strain relations from Navier-Stokes equations
dns_data.exact_relations: pressure Hessian contributes to structure function equations at all orders

new_observables.notes: FNO×RG predicts pressure structure function scaling through the Poisson equation. DNS data on pressure statistics is more limited but qualitatively consistent. The prediction ζ_2^p ≈ 0.93 vs DNS measurement ~0.9±0.1 — agreement within error bars.

new_observables.name: Conditional structure functions

fno_rg_prediction.refined_similarity: S_p(r|ε_r) ~ ε_r^{p/3} r^{p/3} (K62 refined similarity hypothesis)
fno_rg_prediction.fno_rg_correction: SL intermittency modifies the conditional scaling: conditional exponent deviates from p/3 by O(ζ_p correction)
fno_rg_prediction.note: FNO×RG predicts that conditional structure functions given local ε_r should follow modified K62 scaling with SL corrections

dns_data.observation: Velocity increments scale on locally averaged dissipation rate, confirming K62 RSH
dns_data.conditional_scaling: S_2(r|ε_r) ~ ε_r^{2/3} r^{2/3} confirmed to leading order
dns_data.intermittency_modulation: Residual r-dependence after ε_r conditioning reveals intermittency corrections

dns_data.conditional_flatness: F(r|ε_r) reduced compared to unconditional F(r)

dns_data.multifractal_framework: Conditional statistics consistent with multifractal model
dns_data.note: Provides framework for comparison with FNO×RG intermittency predictions

new_observables.notes: FNO×RG framework with SL corrections predicts conditional scaling behavior. DNS confirms K62 RSH to leading order, with intermittency corrections qualitatively consistent with FNO×RG+SL. Quantitative comparison of correction terms requires dedicated analysis.
